1.text: Tha beginning of tha gospel of Jesus Christ, tha Son of God;
As it is written in tha prophets, look, I send my messenger before ur face, which shall prepare ur way before u.
Tha voice of one cryin in tha wilderness, Prepare y’all tha way of tha Lord, make his paths straight.
John did baptize in tha wilderness, N preach tha baptism of repentance 4 tha remission of sins.
N there went out 2 him all tha land of Judæa, N dey of Jerusalem, N were all baptized of him in tha river of Jordan, confessing their sins.
N John was clothed wit camel’s hair, N wit a girdle of a skin about his loins; N he did eat locusts N wild honey;
N preached, sayin, There comes one mightier than I after me, tha latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy 2 stoop down N unloose.
I indeed have baptized u wit water: but he shall baptize u wit tha Holy Ghost.
N it happened in dose days, dat Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, N was baptized of John in Jordan.
N right away comin up out of tha water, he saw tha heavenz opened, N tha Spirit like a dove descending upon him:
N there came a voice from heaven, sayin, u r my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
N right away tha Spirit driveth him in2 tha wilderness.
N he was there in tha wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; N was wit tha wild beasts; N tha angels ministered 2 him.
Now after dat John was put in prison, Jesus came in2 Galilee, preachin tha gospel of tha kingdom of God,
N sayin, tha time is fulfilled, N tha kingdom of God is at hand: repent y’all, N believe tha gospel.
Now as he walked by tha sea of Galilee, he saw Simon N Andrew his brother castin a net in2 tha sea: 4 dey were fishers.
N Jesus said 2 ’em, Come y’all after me, N I will make u 2 become fishers of men.
N right away dey forsook their nets, N followed him.
N when he had gone a little further thence, he saw James tha son of Zebedee, N John his brother, who also were in tha ship mending their nets.
N right away he called ’em: N dey left their father Zebedee in tha ship wit tha hired servants, N went after him.
N dey went in2 Capernaum; N right away on tha sabbath day he entered in2 tha synagogue, N taught.
N dey were astonished at his doctrine: 4 he taught ’em as one dat had authority, N not as tha scribes.
N there was in their synagogue a man wit an unclean spirit; N he cried out,
Sayin, Let us alone; what have we 2 do wit u, u Jesus of Nazareth? r u come 2 destroy us? I know u who u r, tha Holy One of God.
N Jesus rebuked him, sayin, Hold ur peace, N come out of him.
N when tha unclean spirit had torn him, N cried wit a loud voice, he came out of him.
N dey were all amazed, insomuch dat dey questioned among themselves, sayin, What thing is dis? what new doctrine is dis? 4 wit authority commands he even tha unclean spirits, N dey do obey him.
N right away his fame spread abroad throughout all tha region round about Galilee.
N right away, when dey were come out of tha synagogue, dey entered in2 tha house of Simon N Andrew, wit James N John.
But Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever, N anon dey tell him of her.
N he came N took her by tha hand, N lifted her up; N right away tha fever left her, N she ministered 2 ’em.
N at even, when tha sun did set, dey brought 2 him all dat were diseased, N ’em dat were possessed wit devils.
N all tha city was gathered together at tha door.
N he healed many dat were sick of divers diseases, N cast out many devils; N suffered not tha devils 2 speak, because dey knew him.
N in tha morning, risin up a great while before day, he went out, N departed in2 a solitary place, N there prayed.
N Simon N dey dat were wit him followed after him.
N when dey had found him, dey said 2 him, All men seek 4 u.
N he said 2 ’em, Let us go in2 tha next towns, dat I may preach there also: 4 therefore came I forth.
N he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, N cast out devils.
N there came a leper 2 him, beseeching him, N kneeling down 2 him, N sayin 2 him, If u will, u can make me clean.
N Jesus, moved wit compassion, put forth his hand, N touched him, N says 2 him, I will; be u clean.
N as soon as he had spoken, right away tha leprosy departed from him, N he was cleansed.
N he straitly charged him, N right away sent him away;
N says 2 him, See u say nothing 2 any man: but go ur way, show urself 2 tha priest, N offer 4 ur cleansing dose things which Moses commanded, 4 a testimony 2 ’em.

But he went out, N began 2 publish it much, N 2 blaze abroad tha matter, insomuch dat Jesus could no more openly enter in2 tha city, but was without in desert places: N dey came 2 him from every quarter.

2.text: N again he entered in2 Capernaum after some days; N it was noised dat he was in tha house.
N right away many were gathered together, insomuch dat there was no room 2 receive ’em, no, not so much as about tha door: N he preached tha word 2 ’em.
N dey come 2 him, bringin one sick of tha palsy, which was borne of four.
N when dey could not come nigh 2 him 4 tha press, dey uncovered tha roof where he was: N when dey had broken it up, dey let down tha bed in which tha sick of tha palsy lay.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said 2 tha sick of tha palsy, Son, ur sins be forgiven u.
But there were certain of tha scribes sittin there, N reasoning in their hearts,
Why does dis man like dis speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?
N right away when Jesus perceived in his spirit dat dey so reasoned within themselves, he said 2 ’em, Why reason y’all dese things in ur hearts?
Whether is it easier 2 say 2 tha sick of tha palsy, ur sins be forgiven u; or 2 say, Arise, N take up ur bed, N walk?
But dat y’all may know dat tha Son of man has power on earth 2 forgive sins, (he says 2 tha sick of tha palsy,)
I say 2 u, Arise, N take up ur bed, N go ur way in2 thine house.
N right away he arose, took up tha bed, N went forth before ’em all; insomuch dat dey were all amazed, N glorified God, sayin, We never saw it on dis fashion.
N he went forth again by tha sea side; N all tha crowd resorted 2 him, N he taught ’em.
N as he passed by, he saw Levi tha son of Alphæus sittin at tha receipt of custom, N said 2 him, Follow me. N he arose N followed him.
N it happened, dat, as Jesus sat at food in his house, many publicans N sinners sat also together wit Jesus N his disciples: 4 there were many, N dey followed him.
N when tha scribes N Pharisees saw him eat wit publicans N sinners, dey said 2 his disciples, How is it dat he eats N drinks wit publicans N sinners?
When Jesus heard it, he says 2 ’em, dey dat r whole have no need of tha physician, but dey dat r sick: I came not 2 call tha righteous, but sinners 2 repentance.
N tha disciples of John N of tha Pharisees used 2 fast: N dey come N say 2 him, Why do tha disciples of John N of tha Pharisees fast, but ur disciples fast not?
N Jesus said 2 ’em, Can tha children of tha bridechamber fast, while tha bridegroom is wit ’em? as long as dey have tha bridegroom wit ’em, dey cannot fast.
But tha days will come, when tha bridegroom shall be taken away from ’em, N then shall dey fast in dose days.
No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else tha new piece dat filled it up takes away from tha old, N tha rent is made worse.
N no man puts new wine in2 old bottles: else tha new wine does burst tha bottles, N tha wine is spilled, N tha bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put in2 new bottles.
N it happened, dat he went through tha corn fields on tha sabbath day; N his disciples began, as dey went, 2 pluck tha ears of corn.
N tha Pharisees said 2 him, look, why do dey on tha sabbath day dat which is not lawful?
N he said 2 ’em, Have y’all never read what David did, when he had need, N was an hungred, he, N dey dat were wit him?
How he went in2 tha house of God in tha days of Abiathar tha high priest, N did eat tha showbread, which is not lawful 2 eat but 4 tha priests, N gave also 2 ’em which were wit him?
N he said 2 ’em, tha sabbath was made 4 man, N not man 4 tha sabbath:
Therefore tha Son of man is Lord also of tha sabbath.

3.text: N he entered again in2 tha synagogue; N there was a man there which had a withered hand.
N dey watched him, whether he would heal him on tha sabbath day; dat dey might accuse him.
N he says 2 tha man which had tha withered hand, Stand forth.
N he says 2 ’em, Is it lawful 2 do good on tha sabbath days, or 2 do evil? 2 save life, or 2 kill? But dey held their peace.

N when he had looked round about on ’em wit anger, bein grieved 4 tha hardness of their hearts, he says 2 tha man, Stretch forth thine hand. N he stretched it out: N his hand was restored whole as tha other.
N tha Pharisees went forth, N right away took counsel wit tha Herodians against him, how dey might destroy him.
But Jesus withdrew himself wit his disciples 2 tha sea: N a great crowd from Galilee followed him, N from Judæa,
N from Jerusalem, N from Idumaea, N from beyond Jordan; N dey about Tyre N Sidon, a great crowd, when dey had heard what great things he did, came 2 him.
N he spoke 2 his disciples, dat a small ship should wait on him because of tha crowd, lest dey should throng him.
4 he had healed many; insomuch dat dey pressed upon him 4 2 touch him, as many as had plagues.
N unclean spirits, when dey saw him, fell down before him, N cried, sayin, u r tha Son of God.
N he straitly charged ’em dat dey should not make him known.
N he goes up in2 a mountain, N calls 2 him whom he would: N dey came 2 him.
N he ordained twelve, dat dey should be wit him, N dat he might send ’em forth 2 preach,
N 2 have power 2 heal sicknesses, N 2 cast out devils:
N Simon he surnamed Peter;
N James tha son of Zebedee, N John tha brother of James; N he surnamed ’em Boanerges, which is, tha sons of thunder:
N Andrew, N Philip, N Bartholomew, N Matthew, N Thomas, N James tha son of Alphaeus, N Thaddaeus, N Simon tha Canaanite,
N Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: N dey went in2 an house.
N tha crowd comes together again, so dat dey could not so much as eat bread.
N when his friends heard of it, dey went out 2 lay hold on him: 4 dey said, He is beside himself.
N tha scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He has Beelzebub, N by tha prince of tha devils casts he out devils.
N he called ’em 2 him, N said 2 ’em in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?
N if a kingdom be divided against itself, dat kingdom cannot stand.
N if a house be divided against itself, dat house cannot stand.
N if Satan rise up against himself, N be divided, he cannot stand, but has an end.
No man can enter in2 a strong man’s house, N spoil his goods, except he will first bind tha strong man; N then he will spoil his house.
For real I say 2 u, All sins shall be forgiven 2 tha sons of men, N blasphemies wherewith soever dey shall blaspheme:
But he dat shall blaspheme against tha Holy Ghost has never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:
Because dey said, He has an unclean spirit.
There came then his brothers N his mother, N, standin without, sent 2 him, callin him.
N tha crowd sat about him, N dey said 2 him, look, ur mother N ur brothers without seek 4 u.
N he answered ’em, sayin, Who is my mother, or my brothers?
N he looked round about on ’em which sat about him, N said, look my mother N my brothers!
4 whoever shall do tha will of God, tha same is my brother, N my sister, N mother.

4.text: N he began again 2 teach by tha sea side: N there was gathered 2 him a great crowd, so dat he entered in2 a ship, N sat in tha sea; N tha whole crowd was by tha sea on tha land.
N he taught ’em many things by parables, N said 2 ’em in his doctrine,
Listen; look, there went out a sower 2 sow:
N it happened, as he sowed, some fell by tha way side, N tha fowls of tha air came N devoured it up.
N some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; N right away it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth:
But when tha sun was up, it was scorched; N because it had no root, it withered away.
N some fell among thorns, N tha thorns grew up, N choked it, N it yielded no fruit.
N other fell on good ground, N did yield fruit dat sprang up N increased; N brought forth, some thirty, N some sixty, N some an hundred.
N he said 2 ’em, He dat has ears 2 hear, let him hear.
N when he was alone, dey dat were about him wit tha twelve asked of him tha parable.
N he said 2 ’em, 2 u it is given 2 know tha mystery of tha kingdom of God: but 2 ’em dat r without, all dese things r done in parables:
Dat seein dey may see, N not perceive; N hearin dey may hear, N not understand; lest at any time dey should be converted, N their sins should be forgiven ’em.
N he said 2 ’em, Know y’all not dis parable? N how then will y’all know all parables?
Tha sower sows tha word.
N dese r dey by tha way side, where tha word is sown; but when dey have heard, Satan comes right away, N takes away tha word dat was sown in their hearts.
N dese r dey likewise which r sown on stony ground; who, when dey have heard tha word, right away receive it wit gladness;
N have no root in themselves, N so endure but 4 a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution arises 4 tha word’s sake, right away dey r offended.
N dese r dey which r sown among thorns; such as hear tha word,
N tha cares of dis world, N tha deceitfulness of riches, N tha lusts of other things entering in, choke tha word, N it becomes unfruitful.
N dese r dey which r sown on good ground; such as hear tha word, N receive it, N bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, N some an hundred.
N he said 2 ’em, Is a candle brought 2 be put under a bushel, or under a bed? N not 2 be set on a candlestick?
4 there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but dat it should come abroad.
If any man have ears 2 hear, let him hear.
N he said 2 ’em, pay attention what y’all hear: wit what measure y’all mete, it shall be measured 2 u: N 2 u dat hear shall more be given.
4 he dat has, 2 him shall be given: N he dat has not, from him shall be taken even dat which he has.
N he said, So is tha kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed in2 tha ground;
N should sleep, N rise night N day, N tha seed should spring N grow up, he knows not how.
4 tha earth brings forth fruit of herself; first tha blade, then tha ear, after dat tha full corn in tha ear.
But when tha fruit is brought forth, right away he puts in tha sickle, because tha harvest is come.
N he said, Whereunto shall we liken tha kingdom of God? or wit what comparison shall we compare it?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in tha earth, is less than all tha seeds dat be in tha earth:
But when it is sown, it grows up, N becomes greater than all herbs, N shooteth out great branches; so dat tha fowls of tha air may lodge under tha shadow of it.
N wit many such parables spoke he tha word 2 ’em, as dey were able 2 hear it.
But without a parable spoke he not 2 ’em: N when dey were alone, he expounded all things 2 his disciples.
N tha same day, when tha even was come, he says 2 ’em, Let us pass over 2 tha other side.
N when dey had sent away tha crowd, dey took him even as he was in tha ship. N there were also wit him other little ships.
N there arose a great storm of wind, N tha waves beat in2 tha ship, so dat it was now full.
N he was in tha hinder part of tha ship, asleep on a pillow: N dey awake him, N say 2 him, Master, care u not dat we perish?
N he arose, N rebuked tha wind, N said 2 tha sea, Peace, be still. N tha wind ceased, N there was a great calm.
N he said 2 ’em, Why r y’all so fearful? how is it dat y’all have no faith?
N dey feared exceedingly, N said one 2 another, What manner of man is dis, dat even tha wind N tha sea obey him?

5.text: N dey came over 2 tha other side of tha sea, in2 tha country of tha Gadarenes.
N when he was come out of tha ship, right away there met him out of tha tombs a man wit an unclean spirit,
Who had his livin among tha tombs; N no man could bind him, no, not wit chains:
Because dat he had been often bound wit fetters N chains, N tha chains had been plucked asunder by him, N tha fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him.
N always, night N day, he was in tha mountains, N in tha tombs, cryin, N cuttin himself wit stones.
But when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran N worshipped him,
N cried wit a loud voice, N said, What have I 2 do wit u, Jesus, u Son of tha most high God? I adjure u by God, dat u torment me not.
4 he said 2 him, Come out of tha man, u unclean spirit.
N he asked him, What is ur name? N he answered, sayin, My name is Legion: 4 we r many.
N he besought him much dat he would not send ’em away out of tha country.
Now there was there nigh 2 tha mountains a great herd of swine feedin.
N all tha devils besought him, sayin, Send us in2 tha swine, dat we may enter in2 ’em.

N right away Jesus gave ’em leave. N tha unclean spirits went out, N entered in2 tha swine: N tha herd ran violently down a steep place in2 tha sea, (dey were about two thousand;) N were choked in tha sea.
N dey dat fed tha swine fled, N told it in tha city, N in tha country. N dey went out 2 see what it was dat was done.
N dey come 2 Jesus, N see him dat was possessed wit tha devil, N had tha legion, sittin, N clothed, N in his right mind: N dey were afraid.
N dey dat saw it told ’em how it befell 2 him dat was possessed wit tha devil, N also concerning tha swine.
N dey began 2 pray him 2 depart out of their coasts.
N when he was come in2 tha ship, he dat had been possessed wit tha devil prayed him dat he might be wit him.
But Jesus suffered him not, but says 2 him, Go home 2 ur friends, N tell ’em how great things tha Lord has done 4 u, N has had compassion on u.
N he departed, N began 2 publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done 4 him: N all men did marvel.
N when Jesus was passed over again by ship 2 tha other side, much people gathered 2 him: N he was nigh 2 tha sea.
N, look, there comes one of tha rulers of tha synagogue, Jairus by name; N when he saw him, he fell at his feet,
N besought him greatly, sayin, My little daughter lies at tha point of death: I pray u, come N lay ur hands on her, dat she may be healed; N she shall live.
N Jesus went wit him; N much people followed him, N thronged him.
N a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years,
N had suffered many things of many physicians, N had spent all dat she had, N was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,
When she had heard of Jesus, came in tha press behind, N touched his garment.
4 she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.
N right away tha fountain of her blood was dried up; N she felt in her body dat she was healed of dat plague.
N Jesus, right away knowin in himself dat virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in tha press, N said, Who touched my clothes?
N his disciples said 2 him, u see tha crowd thronging u, N sayest u, Who touched me?
N he looked round about 2 see her dat had done dis thing.
But tha woman fearin N tremblin, knowin what was done in her, came N fell down before him, N told him all tha truth.
N he said 2 her, Daughter, ur faith has made u whole; go in peace, N be whole of ur plague.
While he yet spoke, there came from tha ruler of tha synagogue’s house certain which said, ur daughter is dead: why trouble u tha Master any further?
As soon as Jesus heard tha word dat was spoken, he says 2 tha ruler of tha synagogue, don’t be afraid, only believe.
N he suffered no man 2 follow him, save Peter, N James, N John tha brother of James.
N he comes 2 tha house of tha ruler of tha synagogue, N sees tha tumult, N ’em dat wept N wailed greatly.
N when he was come in, he says 2 ’em, Why make y’all dis ado, N weep? tha damsel is not dead, but sleeps.
N dey laughed him 2 scorn. But when he had put ’em all out, he takes tha father N tha mother of tha damsel, N ’em dat were wit him, N enters in where tha damsel was lyin.
N he took tha damsel by tha hand, N said 2 her, Talitha cumi; which is, bein interpreted, Damsel, I say 2 u, arise.
N right away tha damsel arose, N walked; 4 she was of tha age of twelve years. N dey were astonished wit a great astonishment.
N he charged ’em straitly dat no man should know it; N commanded dat something should be given her 2 eat.

6.text: N he went out from thence, N came in2 his own country; N his disciples follow him.

N when tha sabbath day was come, he began 2 teach in tha synagogue: N many hearin him were astonished, sayin, From from where has dis man dese things? N what wisdom is dis which is given 2 him, dat even such mighty works r wrought by his hands?
Is not dis tha carpenter, tha son of Mary, tha brother of James, N Joses, N of Juda, N Simon? N r not his sisters here wit us? N dey were offended at him.
But Jesus said 2 ’em, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, N among his own kin, N in his own house.
N he could there do no mighty work, save dat he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, N healed ’em.
N he marvelled because of their unbelief. N he went round about tha villages, teachin.
N he called 2 him tha twelve, N began 2 send ’em forth by two N two; N gave ’em power over unclean spirits;
N commanded ’em dat dey should take nothing 4 their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse:
But be shod wit sandals; N not put on two coats.
N he said 2 ’em, In what place soever y’all enter in2 an house, there abide till y’all depart from dat place.

N whoever shall not receive u, nor hear u, when y’all depart thence, shake off tha dust under ur feet 4 a testimony against ’em. for real I say 2 u, It shall be more tolerable 4 Sodom N Gomorrha in tha day of judgment, than 4 dat city.
N dey went out, N preached dat men should repent.
N dey cast out many devils, N anointed wit oil many dat were sick, N healed ’em.
N king Herod heard of him; (4 his name was spread abroad:) N he said, dat John tha Baptist was risen from tha dead, N therefore mighty works do show forth themselves in him.
Others said, dat it is Elias. N others said, dat it is a prophet, or as one of tha prophets.
But when Herod heard of it, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he is risen from tha dead.
4 Herod himself had sent forth N laid hold upon John, N bound him in prison 4 Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife: 4 he had married her.
4 John had said 2 Herod, It is not lawful 4 u 2 have ur brother’s wife.
Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, N would have killed him; but she could not:
4 Herod feared John, knowin dat he was a just man N an holy, N observed him; N when he heard him, he did many things, N heard him gladly.
N when a convenient day was come, dat Herod on his birthday made a supper 2 his lords, high captains, N chief estates of Galilee;
N when tha daughter of tha said Herodias came in, N danced, N pleased Herod N ’em dat sat wit him, tha king said 2 tha damsel, Ask of me whatever u will, N I will give it u.
N he sware 2 her, whatever u will ask of me, I will give it u, 2 tha half of my kingdom.
N she went forth, N said 2 her mother, What shall I ask? N she said, tha head of John tha Baptist.
N she came in right away wit haste 2 tha king, N asked, sayin, I will dat u give me by N by in a charger tha head of John tha Baptist.
N tha king was exceeding sorry; yet 4 his oath’s sake, N 4 their sakes which sat wit him, he would not reject her.
N right away tha king sent an executioner, N commanded his head 2 be brought: N he went N beheaded him in tha prison,
N brought his head in a charger, N gave it 2 tha damsel: N tha damsel gave it 2 her mother.
N when his disciples heard of it, dey came N took up his corpse, N laid it in a tomb.
N tha apostles gathered themselves together 2 Jesus, N told him all things, both what dey had done, N what dey had taught.
N he said 2 ’em, Come y’all y’all apart in2 a desert place, N rest a while: 4 there were many comin N goin, N dey had no leisure so much as 2 eat.
N dey departed in2 a desert place by ship privately.
N tha people saw ’em departing, N many knew him, N ran afoot there out of all citiez, N outwent ’em, N came together 2 him.
N Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, N was moved wit compassion toward ’em, because dey were as sheep not havin a shepherd: N he began 2 teach ’em many things.
N when tha day was now far spent, his disciples came 2 him, N said, dis is a desert place, N now tha time is far passed:
Send ’em away, dat dey may go in2 tha country round about, N in2 tha villages, N buy themselves bread: 4 dey have nothing 2 eat.
He answered 2 ’em, Give y’all ’em 2 eat. N dey say 2 him, Shall we go N buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, N give ’em 2 eat?
He says 2 ’em, How many loaves have y’all? go N see. N when dey knew, dey say, Five, N two fishes.
N he commanded ’em 2 make all sit down by companies upon tha green grass.
N dey sat down in ranks, by hundreds, N by fifties.
N when he had taken tha five loaves N tha two fishes, he looked up 2 heaven, N blessed, N broke tha loaves, N gave ’em 2 his disciples 2 set before ’em; N tha two fishes divided he among ’em all.
N dey did all eat, N were filled.
N dey took up twelve baskets full of tha fragments, N of tha fishes.
N dey dat did eat of tha loaves were about five thousand men.
N right away he constrained his disciples 2 get in2 tha ship, N 2 go 2 tha other side before 2 Bethsaida, while he sent away tha people.
N when he had sent ’em away, he departed in2 a mountain 2 pray.
N when even was come, tha ship was in tha midst of tha sea, N he alone on tha land.
N he saw ’em toiling in rowing; 4 tha wind was contrary 2 ’em: N about tha fourth watch of tha night he comes 2 ’em, walkin upon tha sea, N would have passed by ’em.
But when dey saw him walkin upon tha sea, dey supposed it had been a spirit, N cried out:
4 dey all saw him, N were troubled. N right away he talked wit ’em, N says 2 ’em, Be of good cheer: it is I; don’t be afraid.
N he went up 2 ’em in2 tha ship; N tha wind ceased: N dey were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, N wondered.
4 dey considered not tha miracle of tha loaves: 4 their heart was hardened.
N when dey had passed over, dey came in2 tha land of Gennesaret, N drew 2 tha shore.
N when dey were come out of tha ship, right away dey knew him,
N ran through dat whole region round about, N began 2 carry about in beds dose dat were sick, where dey heard he was.

N wherever he entered, in2 villages, or citiez, or country, dey laid tha sick in tha streets, N besought him dat dey might touch if it were but tha border of his garment: N as many as touched him were made whole.

7.text: Then came together 2 him tha Pharisees, N certain of tha scribes, which came from Jerusalem.
N when dey saw some of his disciples eat bread wit defiled, dat is 2 say, wit unwashen, hands, dey found fault.

Makin tha word of God of none effect through ur tradition, which y’all have delivered: N many such like things do y’all.
N when he had called all tha people 2 him, he said 2 ’em, listen 2 me every one of u, N understand:
There is nothing from without a man, dat entering in2 him can defile him: but tha things which come out of him, dose r dey dat defile tha man.
If any man have ears 2 hear, let him hear.
N when he was entered in2 tha house from tha people, his disciples asked him concerning tha parable.
N he says 2 ’em, r y’all so without understanding also? do y’all not perceive, dat whatever thing from without enters in2 tha man, it cannot defile him;
Because it enters not in2 his heart, but in2 tha belly, N goes out in2 tha draught, purging all meats?
N he said, dat which comes out of tha man, dat defiles tha man.
4 from within, out of tha heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:

N from thence he arose, N went in2 tha borders of Tyre N Sidon, N entered in2 an house, N would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.
4 a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, N came N fell at his feet:

N dey bring 2 him one dat was deaf, N had an impediment in his speech; N dey beg him 2 put his hand upon him.
N he took him aside from tha crowd, N put his fingers in2 his ears, N he spit, N touched his tongue;
N lookin up 2 heaven, he sighed, N says 2 him, Ephphatha, dat is, Be opened.

N he charged ’em dat dey should tell no man: but tha more he charged ’em, so much tha more a great deal dey published it;
N were beyond measure astonished, sayin, He has done all things well: he makes both tha deaf 2 hear, N tha dumb 2 speak.

8.text: In dose days tha crowd bein very great, N havin nothing 2 eat, Jesus called his disciples 2 him, N says 2 ’em,

N his disciples answered him, From from where can a man satisfy dese men wit bread here in tha wilderness?

N dey had a few small fishes: N he blessed, N commanded 2 set ’em also before ’em.

N right away he entered in2 a ship wit his disciples, N came in2 tha parts of Dalmanutha.
N tha Pharisees came forth, N began 2 question wit him, seekin of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.
N he sighed deeply in his spirit, N says, Why does dis generation seek after a sign? for real I say 2 u, There shall no sign be given 2 dis generation.
N he left ’em, N entering in2 tha ship again departed 2 tha other side.

N he charged ’em, sayin, pay attention, beware of tha leaven of tha Pharisees, N of tha leaven of Herod.

Havin eyes, see y’all not? N havin ears, hear y’all not? N do y’all not remember?
When I broke tha five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took y’all up? dey say 2 him, Twelve.

N he said 2 ’em, How is it dat y’all do not understand?
N he comes 2 Bethsaida; N dey bring a blind man 2 him, N besought him 2 touch him.

N he sent him away 2 his house, sayin, Neither go in2 tha town, nor tell it 2 any in tha town.
N Jesus went out, N his disciples, in2 tha towns of Cæsarea Philippi: N by tha way he asked his disciples, sayin 2 ’em, Whom do men say dat I am?
N dey answered, John tha Baptist: but some say, Elias; N others, One of tha prophets.
N he says 2 ’em, But whom say y’all dat I am? N Peter answers N says 2 him, u r tha Christ.
N he charged ’em dat dey should tell no man of him.
N he began 2 teach ’em, dat tha Son of man must suffer many things, N be rejected of tha elders, N of tha chief priests, N scribes, N be killed, N after three days rise again.
N he spoke dat sayin openly. N Peter took him, N began 2 rebuke him.
But when he had turned about N looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, sayin, Get u behind me, Satan: 4 u savourest not tha things dat be of God, but tha things dat be of men.
N when he had called tha people 2 him wit his disciples also, he said 2 ’em, whoever will come after me, let him deny himself, N take up his cross, N follow me.
4 whoever will save his life shall lose it; but whoever shall lose his life 4 my sake N tha gospel’s, tha same shall save it.
4 what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain tha whole world, N lose his own soul?
Or what shall a man give in exchange 4 his soul?

Whoever therefore shall be ashamed of me N of my words in dis adulterous N sinful generation; of him also shall tha Son of man be ashamed, when he comes in tha glory of his Father wit tha holy angels.

9.text: N he said 2 ’em, for real I say 2 u, dat there be some of ’em dat stand here, which shall not taste of death, till dey have seen tha kingdom of God come wit power.

N his clothing became shinin, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white ’em.
N there appeared 2 ’em Elias wit Moses: N dey were talking wit Jesus.
N Peter answered 2 Jesus, Master, it is good 4 us 2 be here: N let us make three tabernacles; one 4 u, N one 4 Moses, N one 4 Elias.
4 he knew not what 2 say; 4 dey were sore afraid.
N there was a cloud dat overshadowed ’em: N a voice came out of tha cloud, sayin, dis is my beloved Son: hear him.
N suddenly, when dey had looked round about, dey saw no man any more, save Jesus only wit themselves.

N dey kept dat sayin wit themselves, questioning one wit another what tha risin from tha dead should mean.
N dey asked him, sayin, Why say tha scribes dat Elias must first come?

N when he came 2 his disciples, he saw a great crowd about ’em, N tha scribes questioning wit ’em.
N right away all tha people, when dey beheld him, were greatly amazed, N runnin 2 him greeted him.
N he asked tha scribes, What question y’all wit ’em?
N one of tha crowd answered, Master, I have brought 2 u my son, which has a dumb spirit;
N wherever he takes him, he tears him: N he foameth, N gnasheth wit his teeth, N pineth away: N I spoke 2 ur disciples dat dey should cast him out; N dey could not.
He answers him, N says, O faithless generation, how long shall I be wit u? how long shall I suffer u? bring him 2 me.
N dey brought him 2 him: N when he saw him, right away tha spirit tare him; N he fell on tha ground, N wallowed foaming.
N he asked his father, How long is it ago since dis came 2 him? N he said, Of a child.
N ofttimes it has cast him in2 tha fire, N in2 tha waterz, 2 destroy him: but if u can do any thing, have compassion on us, N help us.

N right away tha father of tha child cried out, N said wit tears, Lord, I believe; help u mine unbelief.

N dey departed thence, N passed through Galilee; N he would not dat any man should know it.
4 he taught his disciples, N said 2 ’em, tha Son of man is delivered in2 tha hands of men, N dey shall kill him; N after dat he is killed, he shall rise tha third day.

10.text: N he arose from thence, N comes in2 tha coasts of Judæa by tha farther side of Jordan: N tha people resort 2 him again; N, as he was wont, he taught ’em again.

u know tha commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Defraud not, Honour ur father N mother.
N he answered 2 him, Master, all dese have I observed from my youth.
Then Jesus beholding him loved him, N said 2 him, One thing u lackest: go ur way, sell whatever u have, N give 2 tha poor, N u will have treasure in heaven: N come, take up tha cross, N follow me.

N dey were in tha way goin up 2 Jerusalem; N Jesus went before ’em: N dey were amazed; N as dey followed, dey were afraid. N he took again tha twelve, N began 2 tell ’em what things should happen 2 him,

N Jesus answered 2 him, What will u dat I should do 2 u? tha blind man said 2 him, Lord, dat I might receive my sight.
N Jesus said 2 him, Go ur way; ur faith has made u whole. N right away he received his sight, N followed Jesus in tha way.

4 for real I say 2 u, dat whoever shall say 2 dis mountain, Be u removed, N be u cast in2 tha sea; N shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe dat dose things which he says shall come 2 pass; he shall have whatever he says.

12.text: N he began 2 speak 2 ’em by parables. A certain man planted a vineyard, N set an hedge about it, N digged a place 4 tha winefat, N built a tower, N let it out 2 husbandmen, N went in2 a far country.

N dey sought 2 lay hold on him, but feared tha people: 4 dey knew dat he had spoken tha parable against ’em: N dey left him, N went their way.

N when dey were come, dey say 2 him, Master, we know dat u r true, N care 4 no man: 4 u regard not tha person of men, but teach tha way of God in truth: Is it lawful 2 give tribute 2 Cæsar, or not?

N dey brought it. N he says 2 ’em, Whose is dis image N superscription? N dey said 2 him, Cæsar’s.
N Jesus answerin said 2 ’em, Render 2 Cæsar tha things dat r Cæsar’s, N 2 God tha things dat r God’s. N dey marvelled at him.
Then come 2 him tha Sadducees, which say there is no resurrection; N dey asked him, sayin,
Master, Moses wrote 2 us, If a man’s brother die, N leave his wife behind him, N leave no children, dat his brother should take his wife, N raise up seed 2 his brother.
Now there were seven brothers: N tha first took a wife, N dyin left no seed.
N tha second took her, N died, neither left he any seed: N tha third likewise.
N tha seven had her, N left no seed: last of all tha woman died also.
In tha resurrection therefore, when dey shall rise, whose wife shall she be of ’em? 4 tha seven had her 2 wife.
N Jesus answerin said 2 ’em, do y’all not therefore err, because y’all know not tha scriptures, neither tha power of God?
4 when dey shall rise from tha dead, dey neither marry, nor r given in marriage; but r as tha angels which r in heaven.
N as touching tha dead, dat dey rise: have y’all not read in tha book of Moses, how in tha bush God spoke 2 him, sayin, I am tha God of Abraham, N tha God of Isaac, N tha God of Jacob?
He is not tha God of tha dead, but tha God of tha livin: y’all therefore do greatly err.
N one of tha scribes came, N havin heard ’em reasoning together, N perceiving dat he had answered ’em well, asked him, Which is tha first commandment of all?
N Jesus answered him, tha first of all tha commandments is, Hear, O Israel; tha Lord our God is one Lord:
N u will love tha Lord ur God wit all ur heart, N wit all ur soul, N wit all ur mind, N wit all ur strength: dis is tha first commandment.
N tha second is like, namely dis, u will love ur neighbour as urself. There is none other commandment greater than dese.
N tha scribe said 2 him, Well, Master, u have said tha truth: 4 there is one God; N there is none other but he:
N 2 love him wit all tha heart, N wit all tha understanding, N wit all tha soul, N wit all tha strength, N 2 love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings N sacrifices.
N when Jesus saw dat he answered discreetly, he said 2 him, u r not far from tha kingdom of God. N no man after dat dared ask him any question.

13.text: N as he went out of tha temple, one of his disciples says 2 him, Master, see what manner of stones N what buildings r here!

y’all have heard tha blasphemy: what think y’all? N dey all condemned him 2 be guilty of death.

15.text: N right away in tha morning tha chief priests held a consultation wit tha elders N scribes N tha whole council, N bound Jesus, N carried him away, N delivered him 2 Pilate.

N dey dat passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, N sayin, Ah, u dat destroy tha temple, N build it in three days,

N when tha sixth hour was come, there was darkness over tha whole land until tha ninth hour.

N Jesus cried wit a loud voice, N gave up tha ghost.
N tha veil of tha temple was rent in twain from tha top 2 tha bottom.

(Who also, when he was in Galilee, followed him, N ministered 2 him;) N many other women which came up wit him 2 Jerusalem.
N now when tha even was come, because it was tha preparation, dat is, tha day before tha sabbath,
